conservation.condition_narrative:
Infrared subtraction (irrsubt) generated responses in the passages of green paint around the edges of the leaves as well as in the stem and spines, suggesting the presence of a blue pigment . These areas appear red in the false color infrared image, which further supports this conclusion. 
Ultraviolet fluorescence (uvl) showed several localized passages of bright orange fluorescence -- notably along the spines of the smaller leaf. This fluorescence color is characteristic of red lake pigments.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Brooklyn Museum of Art in 2025.
